title: Respectable Resilience Despite Big Stock Rally
summary:
Respectable Resilience Despite Big Stock Rally 

             
             
            It ended up being a pleasantly surprising day for the bond market. If the underlying sentiment had been overly bearish, the stock rally gave bonds plenty of cover to move into weaker territory. Instead, the long end of the yield curve made it back into positive territory by the close. By the time we consider that the NASDAQ is barely above the early Nov lows even after today's rally, today's bond market resilience isn't too hard to accept. The bigger question is whether today marks some sort of supportive line in the sand for stocks going forward. From there, any conclusions would need to be tempered, in the short term, by the elevated random volatility risks associated with Thanksgiving week and month-end.

title: Mortgage Rates Just a Hair Higher Despite Early Volatility
summary: Financial markets had an interesting day today with the announcement of Jensen Huang's return as NVDA CEO. It was a bigger deal for stocks with multiple tech names experiencing huge rallies. When the news first came out, it was bad for bonds/rates, but as the day progressed, most of those losses were recovered.  Bonds began the day in stronger territory. This typically points to slightly lower mortgage rates depending on timing. Bonds are moving all night, but mortgage lenders don't set rates for the day until roughly 9:30-10:00am ET.  With the big news coming out at 9am, the timing wasn't great for the mortgage market. Many lenders were forced to set their initial rates higher than last Friday's. As bonds found their footing, many lenders issued mid-day reprices that got the average fairly close to unchanged.   [thirtyyearmortgagerates]

title: AI Mgt., Margin Control, Credit and Verification Tools; STRATMOR on Planning Ahead; RWT's Corporate Moves
summary: Do lenders feel more guilty about the customers they haven’t lent money to, or the ones they’ve lent too much to? There’s a lot going on out there. Several industry vets have suggested to me that there are signs in the current lending environment and guidelines that are similar to 2008. Besides concerns about the immense growth in non-Agency lending, we’re seeing layoffs, packages of servicing rights transferring hands, and the government trying to do things that are “anti-lending.” Take, for example, the VA fee structure news last week, in the misnamed “Take Care of America’s Veteran’s Act.” The government would lead us to believe that this is good news, but the industry is critical. “Vets don’t make a lot of money… so we’re nearly tripling their fees to do a VA IRRL which is supposed to save them money from 50 to 142 basis points?” In another area, ever wonder what Bill Pulte does all day? Critics say he is misguided in targeting faultfinders of the Trump Administration on obscure mortgage issues, while proponents say that rooting out mortgage fraud is “Job 1” for an FHFA director overseeing Freddie and Fannie. title: AM Volatility Following Huang Reinstatement
summary: Stocks were in big trouble on Friday afternoon. Ever since Huang's ouster, the S&P slid from near-all-time-highs to 7-month lows in very short order. NVDA had its worst week since 2008 and was the obvious catalyst for the broader drama. It was likely a busy weekend for the board who came to the conclusion that there was only one conclusion: Huang needed to be reinstated. An hour later and NVDA is up more than 30%. The S&P has more than completely erased Friday's losses. Bonds were several bps stronger before the news but jumped immediately on the Huang news and are now modestly weaker to start the week.

title: Zero-Down FHA Mortgages Get New Look Under Congressional Bill
summary: A new congressional proposal could reopen the debate over FHA's 3.5% minimum down payment, following research suggesting qualified borrowers may not face substantially greater default risk when financing a home with nothing down.The bipartisan Housing Process Parity Act, introduced Nov. 19 by Reps. Young Kim, R-Calif., and Nikema Williams, D-Ga., would direct the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to study the feasibility of zero-down FHA mortgages, including their potential impact on borrowers, housing demand, and the agency's insurance fund.

title: Pennymac Expands Second-Lien Program With Interest-Only Option
summary: Pennymac is expanding its closed-end second mortgage program with a 10-year interest-only payment option and lower credit-score requirements for certain borrowers, giving correspondent lenders more ways to tap home equity without refinancing existing first mortgages.The changes, effective for applications dated Nov. 20 or later, come less than two months after Pennymac launched its standalone second-lien program in September. The lender also announced improvements to certain loan-level price adjustments (LLPAs), effective Nov. 20.

title: CANDID Launches AI Agent That Can Reply to Borrowers Without LO Approval
summary: Mortgage technology company CANDID has launched an AI agent that can respond to borrowers and referral partners without individual LO approval.The Nashville-based company said its new Messaging Agent, now available in beta to CANDID customers, can schedule appointments, generate mortgage scenarios, send pre-approval letters, and create property websites and marketing materials.Unlike conventional messaging assistants, the tool draws on previous text messages, emails, call transcripts, and calendar information to formulate responses based on the borrower's existing relationship with the LO.

title: Mortgage Lending Trails Other Consumer Credit as Borrowing Pressures Mount
summary: Mortgage lending was the exception to an otherwise expanding consumer credit market in October, as Americans continued opening personal loans, credit cards, and auto loans while mortgage originations failed to register year-over-year growth.The latest CreditGauge report from VantageScore highlights the challenges facing originators as consumers continue borrowing for other purposes despite elevated interest rates and affordability pressures.

title: Better Adds Two Mortgage Advisors With $50M in Production to NEO Home Loans
summary: Better Home & Finance Holding Co. has added two mortgage professionals with approximately $50 million in combined historical loan production to its NEO Home Loans channel, continuing its recruitment of experienced originators with established purchase lending businesses.Brandon Goldberg joins as a mortgage advisor in the greater San Diego market, while Ryan Davis joins as a branch leader and mortgage advisor in Lompoc, near Santa Barbara. Together, they bring 22 years of mortgage industry experience.

title: Newrez Survey Finds Self-Employed Buyers Delaying Mortgages
summary: Self-employed borrowers may represent an overlooked source of purchase mortgage business, with many small business owners delaying homebuying because they mistakenly believe they won't qualify for financing, according to a new survey from Newrez.
